candidates.label: Vehicle
candidates.comment: A device designed or used for transporting people or cargo across various environments. Also called conveyance, transport, automobile. Examples: a car, a bicycle, an airplane, a boat, a truck.

candidates.label: Canal
candidates.comment: An artificial waterway constructed for navigation, irrigation, or drainage. Also called waterway, artificial channel, navigation channel. Examples: Panama Canal, Suez Canal, Erie Canal, Grand Canal of China.

candidates.label: TransferAction
candidates.comment: The act of moving an object, whether animate or inanimate, from one location to another. Also called move, transport, relocate. Examples: transferring funds between bank accounts, moving furniture to a new house, transferring a patient to another hospital.

candidates.label: SearchAction
candidates.comment: The act of looking for an object or information, often using a search engine or database. Also called searching, querying, looking up, seeking. Examples: typing a query into Google, searching for a file on a computer, looking up a contact in a directory. Distinct from FindAction, which is the result of a search, not the act itself.

candidates.label: Airline
candidates.comment: An Airline is an Organization that provides air transportation services for passengers. Also called air carrier, air transport company, flight operator. Examples: United Airlines, British Airways, Lufthansa, Southwest Airlines. Distinct from Airport, which is the facility where planes take off and land.

types.oie_definition: A collection of people identified by their shared national origin or citizenship.
types.embedding_query_text: Nationality Group: A collection of people identified by their shared national origin or citizenship. Also called ethnic group, national population, citizen group.

chosen_type.label: StatisticalPopulation
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org 'StatisticalPopulation' class is the best fit, as 'Colombian people' represents a population defined by a specific characteristic.

candidates.label: Taxon
candidates.comment: A cohesive biological unit representing a group of organisms, such as a species, genus, or family. Also called biological classification, taxonomic group, species, genus. Examples: Homo sapiens, Canis familiaris, Felidae (cat family), Plantae (plant kingdom).

candidates.label: StatisticalPopulation
candidates.comment: A set of instances of a given type that satisfy specific constraints, used for statistical analysis. Also called statistical group, data population, sample group, target demographic. Examples: all persons with a home location in a specific city, all events occurring in a particular year, all news articles mentioning a certain keyword. Distinct from StatisticalVariable, which represents a measurable metric within a population.

candidates.label: SizeGroupEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration of common size groups used for various product categories. Also called size category, apparel size group, product size range. Examples: 'Adult', 'Kids', 'Petite', 'Plus Size'.

candidates.label: WearableSizeGroupEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration of common size groups or types for wearable products. Also called apparel size group, clothing size type, garment category. Examples: "men's", "women's", "children's", "unisex".

candidates.label: StatusEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration type representing various status types or states. Also called status list, state types, condition enumeration. Examples: 'Active', 'Pending', 'Completed', 'Cancelled'.

types.oie_definition: A stock or supply of money, materials, staff, and other assets that can be drawn on by a person or organization in order to function effectively.
types.embedding_query_text: Resource: A stock or supply of money, materials, staff, and other assets that can be drawn on by a person or organization in order to function effectively. Also called asset, supply, means.

chosen_type.label: Resource
chosen_type.definition: A stock or supply of money, materials, staff, and other assets that can be drawn on by a person or organization in order to function effectively.
chosen_type.justification: No existing Schema.org type specifically represents a general resource; 'Thing' is the most general suitable parent.

candidates.label: Grant
candidates.comment: A Grant is an intangible, typically financial or quantifiable, allocation of resources from a funder to an organization or person, often supporting specific collective goals or projects. Also called funding award, financial aid, sponsorship, endowment. Examples: research grant, arts grant, student scholarship, disaster relief fund.

candidates.label: Demand
candidates.comment: An intangible entity representing a public announcement by an organization or person seeking specific goods or services. Also called Request for goods, wanted ad, procurement request, call for bids. Examples: A company seeking bids for a new IT system, a person looking to buy a specific vintage car, a job posting for a software engineer. Distinct from Offer, which is an announcement to provide goods or services.

candidates.label: Role
candidates.comment: Additional information describing a relationship or property, such as a person's function in an organization or a character played in a movie. Also called function, capacity, position, part. Examples: 'actor' role for a person in a film, 'member' role for a player on a sports team, 'author' role for a person on a book.

candidates.label: Service
candidates.comment: An intangible offering provided by an organization, such as delivery, consulting, or repair. Also called offering, provision, assistance, support. Examples: a car repair service, a legal consulting service, a package delivery service, a web hosting service.

candidates.label: MonetaryGrant
candidates.comment: An intangible grant that provides a sum of money. Also called financial grant, money award, cash donation. Examples: a research grant, a scholarship, a government subsidy. Distinct from Grant, which can be non-monetary.

types.oie_definition: A measure of the energy released by an earthquake, typically expressed on the Richter or moment magnitude scale.
types.embedding_query_text: Earthquake Magnitude: A measure of the energy released by an earthquake, typically expressed on the Richter or moment magnitude scale. Also called seismic magnitude, quake strength, Richter scale value.

chosen_type.label: EarthquakeMagnitude
chosen_type.definition: A measure of the energy released by an earthquake, typically expressed on the Richter or moment magnitude scale.
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org 'Quantity' class is too broad; 'EarthquakeMagnitude' provides specific classification for this type of measurement.

candidates.label: Energy
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Energy represents a numerical value combined with a unit of energy. Also called power, work, heat. Examples: "100 kWh", "500 Joules", "200 Calories", "1.21 Gigawatts".

candidates.label: Quantity
candidates.comment: Quantity is a data type representing measurable amounts such as distance, time, mass, or weight. Also called amount, measure, magnitude. Examples: '3 kg', '4 milligrams', '10 meters', '2 hours'.

candidates.label: Distance
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Distance represents a numerical value combined with a unit of length. Also called length, extent, span, separation. Examples: "10 km", "5 miles", "300 meters", "2 feet".

candidates.label: Error
candidates.comment: An Error is an InstantaneousEvent representing a problem or failure that occurred. Also called fault, malfunction, issue. Examples: A 404 Not Found error, a database connection error, a system crash, a data validation error.

candidates.label: InstantaneousEvent
candidates.comment: An InstantaneousEvent is a structured value representing an event with no duration, such as a single point in time. Also called momentary event, point event, discrete occurrence. Examples: a computer log entry, a timestamp, a single click on a webpage. Distinct from Event, which typically has a duration.

types.oie_definition: A classification of an earthquake based on its characteristics, such as depth or cause.
types.embedding_query_text: Earthquake Type: A classification of an earthquake based on its characteristics, such as depth or cause. Also called seismic classification, quake category, earthquake class.

chosen_type.label: EarthquakeType
chosen_type.definition: A classification of an earthquake based on its characteristics, such as depth or cause.
chosen_type.justification: No existing Schema.org type represents a type of earthquake; 'QualitativeValue' is a suitable parent for descriptive categories.

candidates.label: BedType
candidates.comment: A QualitativeValue enumeration representing a specific category or style of bed. Also called bed category, bed style, bed size. Examples: "King bed", "Queen bed", "Twin bed", "Sofa bed". Distinct from BedDetails, which describes the quantity and combination of beds.

candidates.label: MapCategoryType
candidates.comment: An enumeration of different categories or kinds of maps. Also called map type, map classification, cartography category. Examples: "RoadMap", "SatelliteMap", "TerrainMap", "HybridMap".

candidates.label: PhysicalActivityCategory
candidates.comment: PhysicalActivityCategory is an enumeration for categories of physical activity, organized by physiologic classification. Also called exercise type, activity classification. Examples: AerobicActivity, StrengthTraining, Flexibility. Distinct from PhysicalActivity, which is an instance of an activity.

candidates.label: MeasurementTypeEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration of common types or dimensions of measurements. Also called dimension type, measurement category, sizing parameter. Examples: "chest circumference", "inseam length", "screw gauge", "wheel diameter".

candidates.label: Volcano
candidates.comment: A landform, typically a mountain, with a vent through which lava, rock fragments, hot vapor, and gas are ejected. Also called active volcano, dormant volcano, volcanic mountain. Examples: Mount Fuji, Mount Vesuvius, Kilauea.

types.oie_definition: A characteristic of matter that can be observed or measured without changing the identity of the substance.
types.embedding_query_text: Physical Property: A characteristic of matter that can be observed or measured without changing the identity of the substance. Also called material property, physical attribute, characteristic.

chosen_type.label: Property
chosen_type.justification: The Schema.org 'Property' class is the best fit, as 'energy' is an attribute or characteristic.

candidates.label: Property
candidates.comment: A Property is an Intangible used to indicate attributes and relationships of some Thing, equivalent to rdf:Property. Also called attribute, characteristic, relation. Examples: "name", "description", "url", "author".

candidates.label: PropertyValue
candidates.comment: A PropertyValue is a StructuredValue representing a property-value pair, such as a feature of a product or place. Also called feature, attribute value, characteristic. Examples: "color: red", "weight: 5kg", "hasWifi: true", "engineType: V8". Distinct from using specific schema.org properties directly, which is preferred when available.

candidates.label: Substance
candidates.comment: Any matter of defined composition with discrete existence, which can be biological, mineral, or chemical. Also called material, chemical compound, element, matter. Examples: water, oxygen, penicillin, granite.

candidates.label: PropertyValueSpecification
candidates.comment: A PropertyValueSpecification is an Intangible defining the specification for a property's value. Also called value constraint, property definition. Examples: a specification for the allowed range of a numerical property, a definition of valid input for a text field, a schema for a complex property value.

candidates.label: LocationFeatureSpecification
candidates.comment: A structured value that specifies a feature of an accommodation, represented as a property-value pair. Also called accommodation feature, amenity detail, property value specification. Examples: "hasWifi: true", "numberOfBedrooms: 3", "petsAllowed: false", "poolType: outdoor".
